papers.title: See2Think: Do Multimodal Models Really Use Intermediate Visual States?
papers.desc: Multimodal large language models increasingly use sketches, annotations, tools, and intermediate images during reasoning, but it remains unclear whether they truly rely on these visual states.

papers.title: β-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation
papers.desc: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) is a promising approach to improve reasoning language models, but it remains brittle in practice: making it work reliably often requires substantial engineering effort.

papers.title: ShadowDancer: Teaching Video World Models Any Action by Learning Unified Dynamics Representations from a Video and Its Shadow
papers.desc: We present ShadowDancer, a novel approach to any-action, frame-level control of interactive video world models.

papers.title: INTACT: Isomorphic Intent-to-Action Learning for Search-Free World Models
papers.desc: Forward latent world models predict how actions change a scene, but recover actions for a desired change only through expensive test-time search.

papers.title: Σ-Mem: An Online Reliability Memory for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
papers.desc: Memory is central to long-horizon LLM agents, yet existing memory systems primarily preserve interaction content rather than modeling which agents can be trusted and under what conditions.

papers.title: LEDGERMIND: Provenance-Constrained Multimodal Agentic Reasoning with a Structured Evidence Ledger
papers.desc: Multimodal agents for visual question answering increasingly operate as multi-step trajectories that interleave perception, retrieval, and reasoning, yet evaluation still largely reduces to final-answer accuracy.

papers.title: Explorative Modeling: Unlocking a Third Pretraining Axis and End-to-End Generation
papers.desc: The deep learning revolution, kicked off by AlexNet, taught us that end-to-end training beats decomposing a problem into hand-designed stages.

papers.title: Multi-Head Attention Residuals
papers.desc: Transformers propagate information across depth through a single additive residual stream: every sublayer reads only the most recent state.

papers.title: Filesystem-Based Memory for LLM Agents: Organization, Evolution, and Sustainability
papers.desc: Deployed LLM agents increasingly keep their long-term memory as a filesystem: a directory tree of markdown files that the agent itself reads, writes, and reorganizes through generic file tools.

papers.title: OmniScope: Modality-Decoupled Token Compression for Omnimodal Large Language Models
papers.desc: Existing token compression methods for omnimodal large language models typically rely on one modality to determine what to retain in the other.

papers.title: Is Deep Research Reliable? Misleading Knowledge Induces False Conclusions
papers.desc: Deep Research agents extend LLM-based assistants into long-horizon workflows involving planning, retrieval, evidence synthesis, and report generation, yet their reliability in open information environments remains underexplored.

papers.title: Beyond Geometric Complementarity: Coherent Overlap in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Routing
papers.desc: Sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models route each token to multiple experts, suggesting a geometric account of their benefit: co-selected experts should contribute distinct representation directions.

papers.title: Fairness Pruning: Locating Demographic Bias in GLU-MLP Layers via Differential Activations
papers.desc: This work presents Fairness Pruning, a lightweight structural intervention method designed for the management and future mitigation of demographic bias in large language models (LLMs).

papers.title: Pedestrian Archetypes Extension -- More Pedestrian Models for Autonomous Vehicle Safety Testing
papers.desc: In our prior work, Pedestrian Archetypes, we defined pedestrian archetypes as collections of behaviors that uniquely identify a specific type of pedestrian.

papers.title: AMRD: Adaptive Multi-Teacher Relational Distillation for Lightweight Speech Emotion Recognition
papers.desc: On-device speech emotion recognition (SER) is critical for real-time applications, yet large self-supervised models that excel at SER are too costly for edge devices.
